articles.title: El Arsenal lo quiere todo: Mikel Merino, Dowman y Madueke invitan a otra ronda
articles.standfirst: Los 'gunners', que lo han ganado todo este curso, avanzan a octavos de la Copa de la Liga
articles.summary: Los 'gunners', que lo han ganado todo este curso, avanzan a octavos de la Copa de la Liga
articles.body: El Arsenal no distingue. Le da igual Premier, Champions... que Carabao Cup. Lo quiere todo. Conquistó la Supercopa inglesa frente al Manchester City (3-0) y cuenta sus siete partidos por victorias en este inicio de curso. La última, frente al recién ascendido Ipswich Town (2-4) para avanzar a octavos de la Copa de la Liga. Poco importó que Mikel Arteta rotara a ¡nueve! de los titulares que derrotaron al Sunderland (0-2) en Liga. Sólo repitieron Gabriel Magalhaes y Lewis-Skelly. Dio entrada, en cambio, a Salmon, Bruno Guimaraes, Madueke, Dowman, Eze, Gyökeres... y tres de los 'nuestros'. Alineó de inicio a Kepa, Mikel Merino y Zubimendi, al que volvió a colocar como improvisado lateral derecho. No le hizo falta al Arsenal sacar su mejor fútbol. Le bastó con presionar la defectuosa salida de balón del Ipswich. Así llegaron los dos primeros goles. Max Dowman 'abrió la lata' en el 7': recuperó el balón, tiró la pared con Eze, sentó a Kipré y batió mano a mano a Walton. El 0-2, en el 16', siguió el mismo guion. Bruno Guimaraes se lanzó con todo para interceptar una mala entrega del meta, Mikel Merino filtró un excepcional pase de primeras para Noni Madueke y el extremo inglés fusiló de zurda. El 0-3 llegó en el 47', nada más iniciarse el segundo tiempo, esta vez tras una jugada elaborada con acento español. Zubimendi filtró adentro hacia Max Dowman y la gran 'joya' 'gunner' (16 años) resolvió con un tiro ajustado al palo largo. Mikel Merino se sumó a la fiesta en el 58'. Bruno Guimaraes encontró en la frontal al internacional español y el ex de la Real Sociedad resolvió con un tiro ajustado al poste. Tan ajustado que golpeó en el palo. Es su primer gol del curso. Anis Mehmeti recortó distancias para el Ipswich en el 62'. Desbordó de maravilla por izquierda el recién ingresado Jack Clarke y cedió atrás para que el albanés rematara a placer. Chuba Akpom anotó el definitivo 2-4 en el 91'. Centró Leif Davis desde la izquierda y marcó el excanterano del Arsenal con algo de suerte: su disparo golpeó en Ezri Konsa y despistó a Kepa.

Pellegrino materializó el 1-0 tras un mal despeje del meta visitante y, ya en la segunda parte, Gnonto sentenció. Cerró la goleada, ya en el descuento, Pedro Gonçalves con un buen disparo desde la frontal. La Fiore, mientras, saca la cabeza del hoyo tras un arranque de curso desastroso (tres partidos de Serie A, tres derrotas) que le costó el puesto a Fabio Grosso. Con Vanoli, la vida es de otro color... pero el calendario no da tregua. Precisamente, como en un futuro en Coppa, se medirán al Nápoles este fin de semana por el campeonato italiano.

articles.title: Omonia Nicosia - Celta | Europa para la depresión: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: El Celta busca romper su mala dinámica en su visita a Chipre
articles.summary: El Celta busca romper su mala dinámica en su visita a Chipre
articles.body: Disputar competición europea puede convertirse, en ocasiones, una distracción o una presión añadida que termina por pasar factura en el torneo doméstico. En otras, puede servir más bien para todo lo contrario: elevar la moral y recuperar la confianza de un equipo que transita con pena por el resto de competiciones. Y este último es el caso de un Celta que, hundido en la clasificación y sin conocer la victoria en liga, busca un triunfo balsámico en Chipre que le devuelva la sonrisa. Más allá del factor anímico, basta echar un vistazo al calendario de los de Giráldez en esta Europa League para saber que la salida a Nicosia es casi una obligación de éxito si quiere aspirar a seguir adelante en la competición. Marsella o Glasgow se antojan, a priori, mucho más difíciles para sacar algo positivo. Por poner dos claros ejemplos de lo que le espera al equipo celeste en esta fase de liguilla donde será clave atar los puntos de casa. En el aspecto meramente deportivo, el equipo viaja con un sabor agridulce en cuanto al capítulo de altas y bajas. Borja Iglesias vuelve a entrar en la convocatoria, aunque no está previsto que salga de inicio para paliar la ausencia del gran capitán, Iago Aspas. Su ausencia reduce aún más las opciones ofensivas para Giráldez en un equipo que no anda sobrado de gol precisamente. Con todo, el técnico celeste tiene pensado continuar con su política de rotaciones y dar entrada a algunos de los menos habituales en los encuentros disputados hasa ahora en LaLiga. Está previsto que se produzca el estreno bajo palos del turco Bayindir en lugar de Radu. El Omonia Nicosia, por su parte, ha comenzado con ciertas dudas la temporada tras firmar dos empates en sus tres partidos de liga. Algo que viene a ratificar la visita a Chipre como el escenario idóneo para que el Celta busque reencontrarse con su mejor versión... y con un gran resultado.

articles.title: Northern Ireland: Squad only picked on merit says Michael O'Neill
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says he would never take Fifa eligibility rules into consideration when selecting his squad.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill has said he would never take Fifa eligibility rules into consideration when selecting his squad.

Reaching four senior caps for a country rules out a future switch of international allegiance with the regulations again in the spotlight with regards to Arsenal teenager Ceadach O'Neill.

The 18-year-old won his first two Northern Ireland caps in June friendlies against Guinea and France, and is in the squad for an upcoming Nations League quadruple-header, but has also been subject to an approach from the Republic of Ireland.

After stating that he does not feel it is fair to ask teenagers to make "irreversible" decisions on their international future, Michael O'Neill said he would not consider bringing players into the squad with a view to tying them to Northern Ireland before other associations show interest.

"I wouldn't just put a player on the pitch for that because that would be unfair on the player and I've never done that," he said.

"I've never put a player on the pitch from that point of view. I've always tried to be fair across the board if players deserve the opportunity to play, which Ceadach did.

"Because he trained so well, he got the opportunity to play."

Northern Ireland's latest Nations League campaign starts away to Georgia on 25 September and Ceadach O'Neill is one of four teenagers in the squad alongside Blackburn Rovers defender Tom Atcheson, Everton forward Braiden Graham and Kieran Morrison - the Liverpool winger currently on loan at Sheffield Wednesday.

Atcheson and Morrison were both born in England but qualify for Northern Ireland through grandparents and represented the side at underage level before making their senior bows in March and June respectively.

"Kieran deserved the chance to play because he'd been around the Liverpool first team. He'd been showing up well in training as well, both in March and June," said O'Neill after naming a 28-man squad for the four-game window.

"Braiden is the same. They're there because this is the next step for them. I believe being part of the senior international squad will help them, will help their club careers, but they merit a place in a 28-man squad. They merit their place in that squad over some players that aren't in my opinion.

"My job is to protect the national team going forward and to build the squad as strong as possible. To do that you have to look at your young players."

Entrusting young players with key roles, in many cases before they are established at their club sides, has been common practice for Northern Ireland in recent years.

Conor Bradley, Isaac Price and the Charles brothers, Shea and Pierce, all made their international debuts as teenagers, while Sunderland pair Dan Ballard and Trai Hume broke into the side as 20-year-olds.

O'Neill himself won his first cap at 18 in 1988 and cited Norman Whiteside making an international debut as a 17-year-old at the 1982 World Cup as another example of how the side relied on early exposure for young players long before any eligibility issues came to the fore.

"This is not new for Northern Ireland. We've done this in the past," he added.

"I understand how this works. We're doing it based on the level of the player and that's the most important thing."

articles.title: El Liverpool de Iraola da la estocada al Tottenham con un golazo de Szoboszlai
articles.standfirst: Mac Allister, Gakpo y Szoboszlai 'invalidaron' en gol del exrojiblanco Gallagher para los 'Spurs'
articles.summary: Mac Allister, Gakpo y Szoboszlai 'invalidaron' en gol del exrojiblanco Gallagher para los 'Spurs'
articles.body: El Tottenham, que evitó el descenso 'in extremis' la temporada pasada, no termina de arrancar... a pesar de haberse gastado 366 millones de euros en fichajes este verano. Los 'Spurs', cuartos por la cola, no saben aún lo que es marcar en Premier. Por si fuera poco, los de Roberto de Zerbi han caído eliminados ante el Liverpool (3-1) en dieciseisavos de la Copa de la Liga. A los 21' ya ganaban los de Andoni Iraola, que alineó de inicio a Mamardashvili y Ronald Araujo, esta vez como central; y dejó en el banquillo a Víctor Muñoz. Alexis Mac Allister, llegando desde atrás, recogió un balón muerto en la frontal y la 'clavó' en la escuadra con la diestra. El 'Pool' bailó al Tottenham para anotar el 2-0 en el 54'. Recibió Cody Gakpo de Mac Allister tras una larga jugada colectiva y resolvió con un derechazo al palo largo. Está en forma el neerlandés, que suma dos goles y tres asistencias. Recortó distancias Conor Gallagher en el 69'. El ex del Atlético forzó un saque de esquina y, acto seguido, cabeceó a la red el córner servido por Mateus Fernandes. De poco sirvió. El Liverpool le dio la 'estocada' al Tottenham en el 91'. El húngaro recibió de Cody Gakpo, controló con el pecho y conectó un espectacular obús desde 35 metros imparable para Martin Dubravka.

articles.summary: Before the game Mikel Arteta said Max Dowman "will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else".  Last season the teenager played 13 tim...
articles.body:
Before the game Mikel Arteta said Max Dowman "will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else".

Last season the teenager played 13 times - and became the youngest Premier League scorer ever against Everton - but had just been an unused substitute this season so far.

He earned those minutes and more at Portman Road - and will surely be getting another chance in the league soon.

His two goals showed different attributes, first of all displaying great skill and good pace to run at Ipswich's defence and finish. For the second one he was alert in the box to receive a pass and then kept his cool to pick his spot.

Dowman also let the ball run to Mikel Merino for his strike to make it 4-0.

He is just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side in any competition, after Wayne Rooney for Everton against Wrexham in 2002 - also in the League Cup.

articles.title: Sterling admite los cargos de conducción peligrosa y posesión de drogas
articles.standfirst: El internacional inglés, sin equipo, tuvo un accidente con su coche el 28 de mayo
articles.summary: El internacional inglés, sin equipo, tuvo un accidente con su coche el 28 de mayo
articles.body: El futbolista Raheem Sterling, cuyo último equipo fue el Feyenoord, ha admitido los cargos de conducción peligrosa y de posesión de drogas después de que sufriera un accidente de coche en mayo de este año. Sterling, de 31 años, se encuentran sin equipo desde que pasara seis meses en el Feyenoord la temporada pasada. El jugador tuvo un accidente en su Lamborghini el pasado 28 de mayo y, según lo declarado en los juzgados de Basingstoke, fue detenido y arrestado después de que varios testigos alertaran a la policía preocupados por su estado al volante. Sterling, que admitió tener un problema con el óxido nitroso, fue encontrado en el asiento del pasajero con varios botes de esta droga, así como un globo para poder inhalarlo. La posesión de esta sustancia, conocida como gas de la risa, está penada en Inglaterra desde 2023. El futbolista se ha declarado culpable del cargo de conducción peligrosa, del de posesión de drogas y de uno adicional por no haber podido dar una muestra de su aliento. En las próximas semanas se conocerá su sentencia.

articles.title: Quique: "Hemos jugado contra un equipo que tiene mejores jugadores de lo que dice la clasificación"
articles.standfirst: El técnico cree que el empate hubiera sido el resultado más justo
articles.summary: El técnico cree que el empate hubiera sido el resultado más justo
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores compareció ante los medios de comunicación para hacer un balance de la derrota ante el Valencia en Mendizorroza. El técnico reconoció que el rival aprovechó el ‘factor sorpresa’ para entrar mejor al partido, aunque cree que su equipo hizo méritos para sumar un punto. Análisis: “En los primeros 15 minutos nos ha costado ajustar la posición de Javi Guerra con el cuadrado que han hecho en el centro del campo. No sabíamos cómo iban a situarse con el nuevo entrenador. A partir del minuto 15 hemos fluido igual que el Valencia. Nosotros a través del centro lateral y ellos con balones a la espalda. El partido ha sido así hasta el final. En el segundo tiempo se ha acentuado el dominio, pero ellos son un equipo muy peligroso al contragolpe. El gol es una maniobra excelente de Javi Guerra. Estamos muy expuestos en Primera y cualquier maniobra puede poner en riesgo el partido”. Falta de reacción en la recta final: “Hemos atacado con bastantes jugadores por detrás de la pelota. Ha habido situaciones que hemos atacado contra once jugadores. Hemos estado bien cuando hemos atacado en velocidad contra menos jugadores. Ellos después del gol nos han concedido la pelota y no hemos sido tan prácticos ni peligrosos. Ha sido un partido que se ha decantado en un detalle de calidad, pero hemos merecido sacar un punto. Ha sido el partido que esperábamos en estadísticas y en sensaciones”. Valencia: “Hemos jugado contra un equipo que tiene mejores jugadores de lo que dice la clasificación y tiene cuatro o cinco jugadores de un nivel muy alto que son capaces de girarte un partido”. Factor sorpresa: “Ellos han hecho un cuadrado con dos mediocentros y dos jugadores como Javi Guerra y Ugrinic. Para un 4-4-2 como el nuestro no era fácil llegar a los balones. Guido es un jugador que les viene muy bien y les da mucho criterio. Ha metido tres o cuatro diagonales con mucho peligro y ponía en ventaja a Danjuma. Lo peor que podía pasarnos era no saber que estructura de ataque iban a elegir y poder rectificar esa dificultad ante la marcha”. Dos derrotas consecutivas: “El riesgo de poder perder va a estar todo el tiempo. Somos un equipo humilde, que trabaja y pelea, pero los detalles lo van a decidir. Hoy el detalle los ha puesto un jugador como Guerra y lo ha rematado Rioja, que aquí en Vitoria era diferencial. De momento estamos bien en la clasificación. Mañana nos levantaremos un poco más tristes, pero hay que seguir porque dentro de 4 días tenemos otra tarea complicada en San Mamés”. Apartado físico: “Hemos empezado el partido con cinco jugadores que no habían jugado más de 45 minutos el sábado. Nos ha cambiado bastante el gol del Valencia porque hemos tenido que sacar a jugadores que estaban prácticamente sin calentar. Mariano y Yusi han entrado en un buen momento del partido. Hay jugadores que no acaban de estar bien físicamente porque se han lesionado en un momento de la temporada en la que es importante estar bien”. Primer partido sin gol: “Es doloroso no marcar porque estamos acostumbrados a hacerlo. Hemos tirado 16 veces y el arreón lo hemos tenido. Estamos tirando bastante. Otra cosa es que no se dignifique tanto porque las ocasiones no acaben siendo tan peligrosas. No estamos teniendo ese acierto en los últimos partidos”.

articles.title: John Stones forced off in first Inter Milan start as Cristian Chivu provides update
articles.summary: John Stones was forced off during Inter Milan's 5-3 win over Udinese on Monday, with team boss Cristian Chivu having now provided an injury update on the for...
articles.body:
Inter Milan manager Cristian Chivu has confirmed John Stones "felt something in his flexor" that necessitated his withdrawal during a 5-3 victory against Udinese . The former Manchester City center-back was making his maiden start on Monday following his move to the Italian champions but departed the San Siro early due to a suspected problem.

Stones pulled up while pursuing Keinan Davis and gestured to the bench before subsequently being substituted by Benjamin Pavard .

Curtis Jones also entered the match when Stones departed, with the former Liverpool midfielder enjoying an impressive beginning at Inter compared to the latter and fellow Englishman Djed Spence , as per the Manchester Evening News .

The ex-Tottenham Hotspur fullback has yet to appear due to injury, while both Jones and Stones delivered respectable performances against Real Madrid in the UEFA Champions League last week.

Stones may now face a period on the treatment table, with his fitness concerns during his final campaigns at City suggesting it's improbable he'll recover quickly. Inter will travel to face AS Roma in their last match before the international break.

The break could prove invaluable for rest and recovery, though Thomas Tuchel will almost certainly want him involved in England 's Nations League fixtures against Spain , Croatia , and the Czech Republic twice.

Stones has been utilized in the center of a back three, with Chivu previously highlighting the experience he and Jones bring to the side, having made history for Inter in the victory over Cagliari as the first occasion the club fielded two English players simultaneously.

He stated in late August: "They're experienced players who are comfortable playing under pressure in certain matches. I have nothing to reproach them for their attitude, they are two exemplary guys who give everything and I'm happy to have them."

Multiple Premier League clubs expressed interest in securing the 32-year-old's signature at the expiration of his City contract before Inter entered the picture and quickly convinced Stones to make the move.

Having claimed countless honors during his decade under Pep Guardiola, Stones was gradually eased out of the setup, with January signing Marc Guehi appearing to have taken his place.

Bernardo Silva also departed on a free transfer to Real Madrid, while City generated revenue through the sales of Savio to Tottenham, Rodri to Barcelona , and Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah, among numerous other notable departures.

City's financial flexibility enabled them to splash out on Enzo Fernandez and Iliman Ndiaye , both of whom proved instrumental in their commanding Manchester derby triumph, despite losing Phil Foden to a red card in just the 23rd minute.

Erling Haaland struck the decisive goal in contentious circumstances, with Fernandez escaping an offside ruling despite visibly attempting to play the ball while positioned beyond the last defender.

With a changing of the guard coming for the national team, this is an excellent choice to give the young talents in Germany the opportunity to fix Die Mannschaft and set the nation back on track to the top of world football.

articles.title: West Ham 2-3 Fulham: Super-sub Oscar Bobb the difference-maker as Alvaro Arbeloa's side edge thrilling London derby
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup third-round tie between West Ham and Fulham at the London Stadium; Oscar Bobb came off the bench to send Alvaro Arbeloa's side through
articles.body:
The visitors were pegged back twice at the London Stadium, but super-sub Oscar Bobb made the difference to hand Alvaro Arbeloa his second win as Cottagers boss.

Prior to the game, the Hammers held a period of appreciation in honour of former goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko, who passed away following a battle with cancer.

Latest news and rumours: West Ham | Fulham

West Ham had scored 27 goals this season prior to the tie, while Fulham had conceded three in two of their four Premier League games, so it was no surprise to see a goal-fest quickly commence.

After a dominant start, Rodrigo Muniz headed the visitors ahead after some lacklustre defending from the home side. However, that lead lasted less than three minutes, as some equally poor defending from a set-piece resulted in an easy header for Morato.

Normal service continued after the equaliser, and having missed two good chances beforehand, Cesar Palacios finally applied the finishing touch with a classy poke past Finlay Herrick.

Yet, in a case of deja vu, back came West Ham as Pablo smashed in his long-awaited first Hammers goal seconds before the break.

Both sides sent on the big guns in search of the winner. Jarrod Bowen and Taty Castellanos entered for the hosts, but it was Fulham's changes that made the difference. Josh King won possession on the edge of the West Ham box, before Bobb danced his way into the area and slotted home for his first goal for the club.

The aforementioned West Ham duo combined for what surely had to be the equaliser as Bowen squared to Castellanos for a tap-in. However, the Spaniard was far too casual, allowing Timothy Castagne to clear off the line and ensure Fulham made it through.

articles.title: Bristol City 0-1 Lincoln City: Freddie Draper scores Imps winner in narrow victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bristol City and Lincoln City at Ashton Gate on Tuesday night; Freddie Draper nets as Imps win at new home of their old boss Michael Skubala.
articles.body:
The decisive moment came on 53 minutes when Ben House intercepted Rob Dickie's miscued back-pass, which left goalkeeper Sam Tickle stranded, and set up Draper to shoot into an unguarded net.

The home side fought hard to level but Lincoln, promoted under Skubala last season, defended strongly to show how well they have adapted to life at the higher level.

Bristol City gave a home debut to 22-year-old Dutch midfielder Gibson Yah as one of three changes to the team beaten 4-1 at Southampton, while Lincoln made five changes from their 1-0 victory at Preston including a first League start for Chiedozie Ogbene supporting lone striker Draper.

All the meaningful action in a competitive first half that saw five players cautioned came in the opening half-hour. Lincoln were first to threaten when Draper's low drive on four minutes was parried by Tickle.

Yu Hirakawa had a similar effort dealt with by Lincoln keeper George Wickens two minutes later before Bristol City came within inches of taking an 11th-minute lead.

Rio Cardines went into the match with five assists already this season and his pinpoint corner from the left saw Lorent Tolaj direct a powerful header against the crossbar.

Yah had a header deflected for a corner and Tolaj sliced wide at the far post from another Cardines cross before Lincoln went close on 27 minutes, Ogbene nodding wide at the near post after referee Tim Robinson had played a good advantage.

From then until the break, both sides struggled to create openings as the yellow card count mounted.

Draper's goal rewarded Lincoln for a bright start to the second half that saw Deji Elerewe glance a header wide while Ogbene had a low shot saved.

Draper fired over from distance with his team well on top and Lincoln fans taunting their former manager. But it took an outstretched leg from keeper George Wickens to protect the Imps' lead when Hirakawa was presented with a great chance on the hour.

Skubala had just replaced Jed Wallace with Dom Ballard in a bid to add potency up front.

Dickie's night to forget was ended by injury on 72 minutes, Rob Atkinson taking over as his fellow centre-back was stretchered off following a challenge from behind.

Bristol built some pressure and Yah's close-range shot was blocked following another Cardines corner.

The best the hosts could offer after that was an injury time effort from Ballard that passed harmlessly wide and home supporters were quick to voice their frustration at the final whistle.

articles.title: Middlesbrough 2-2 Millwall: Will Lankshear scores equaliser as Boro battle back for a point
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Middlesbrough and Millwall at the Riverside Stadium on Tuesday night; Amario Cozier-Duberry and Will Lankshear score as Boro fight back for a point, but they miss the chance to go top of the table.
articles.body:
The Lions deservedly led by two goals at the break after capitalising on Boro's unconvincing start.

Strike duo Tairyk Arconte and Lyndon Dykes put Millwall in the driving seat after finding the net in the 11th and 36th minutes respectively.

But Middlesbrough, who controlled possession for most of the game, recovered to claim a point after head coach Kim Hellberg made three changes at half-time.

The excellent Amario Cozier-Duberry scored his second goal since arriving on loan from Brighton in the 50th minute, before striker Will Lankshear headed in his eighth of the season to equalise just after the hour.

That result lifted Middlesbrough to third place, despite breaking their 100 per cent home record.

Millwall took the early lead when Arconte, signed from French Ligue 2 side Rodez in the summer, darted past Luke Ayling before cutting back and striking low in off Radek Vitek's near post.

The 22-year-old's third goal of the season seemed the perfect response to Millwall's recent away slump, which had seen them concede eight goals on their last two trips.

Hellberg's side controlled most of the play after that opener, forcing Millwall to defend strongly.

Middlesbrough's closest chance in the opening half-hour was when Max Crocombe turned Lankshear's scrappy back-post volley over the bar.

But Middlesbrough looked threatened by the presence of Arconte and Dykes.

After conceding a corner just before half-time, the home side found themselves two goals down after failing to clear the ball into the box.

Jenson Metcalfe's delivery was met by Derek Mazou-Sacko's downward header, which Caleb Taylor flicked back across goal for Dykes, left out of new coach Sebastien Pocognoli's first Scotland squad, to turn in.

Hellberg disliked what he saw and introduced substitutes Kyle Joseph, Max Arfsten and Jeremy Sarmiento for the second half.

Within minutes Crocombe had to dive to his right to save a curling effort from Cozier-Duberry that energised the home fans.

Cozier-Duberry did not wait long for a goal. After Millwall failed to deal with a corner effectively, the London-born trickster's deflected effort hit the net.

Middlesbrough had lift-off. Just after the hour Lankshear headed in Ayling's deep cross to the back post to level the score.

Yet Vitek still had to make a point-blank save to stop substitute Elkan Baggott from heading Millwall back in front.

After that, the question was whether Middlesbrough would win it. Cozier-Duberry had a couple of chances, while Sarmiento curled an effort just wide of the upright as Millwall survived with a point.

What the result means and next fixtures...
